claims.evidence: The witness report confirms they are used tires but cannot verify the 'grade' or import status.
The report notes a directional pattern but no millimeter measurement or depth gauge was used.
The inner condition of the tire was not shown to the witness.
Only one side of the tire is visible; internal belt separation or opposite sidewall bulges are not ruled out.
The DOT manufacturing date code is missing from the report.

risks.risk: Tire age (Dry rot or structural failure)
risks.proof: A clear photo of the 4-digit DOT code on the sidewall.

risks.risk: Hidden internal repairs or sidewall damage
risks.proof: A video or photo of the entire inner liner of the tire.
risks.if_unproven: as having at least one major patch.

risks.risk: Incorrect size for the buyer's vehicle
risks.proof: A photo of the sidewall markings showing width, aspect ratio, and rim diameter (e.g., 205/55R16).
risks.if_unproven: as the smallest/cheapest common rim size.

proof_requests: Photo of the full sidewall showing the size (e.g., 195/65R15)
Photo of the 4-digit DOT date code
Photo of the tire's interior (inner liner)
Photo of tread depth measurement using a gauge or a coin for scale
response.reason: The tire size and manufacturing date are not visible; without the size, it is impossible to assign even a worst-case price as the rim diameter determines the price category.
